items.summary:
GOOGLE IS QUIETLY GIVING AWAY 15 AI TOOLS AND MOST PEOPLE ONLY KNOW GEMINI

The five worth your afternoon:

Pomelli — paste your website URL. It pulls your fonts, colors and tone, then builds a full social campaign that actually looks like your brand.

Stitch — one sentence in, production-ready UI and websites out. Still in beta and already replacing paid mockup tools.

Opal — n8n or Make, except Google's AI is baked in. Describe the workflow, it wires it up. No code.

Antigravity — an agentic code editor on Gemini 3 Pro. He asked for a flight lookup app, the agents planned it, built it, then generated the landing page for it too.

Mixboard — infinite canvas for images. Generate, remix, merge the parts you like, keep going until it matches what's in your head.

Brand, design, automation, code, visuals. Five tabs, zero dollars.

Most people are paying monthly for all five. Why?

items.title: Most people know Google AI for Gemini.
items.summary:
Most people know Google AI for Gemini.

What they don’t realize is that Google has quietly released a whole ecosystem of powerful AI tools—many of them completely free.

Here are five worth trying today:

• Pomelli — Paste your website URL, and it instantly analyzes your brand’s fonts, colors, and tone to generate a complete social media campaign that actually matches your identity.

• Stitch — Describe your idea in one sentence, and it turns it into production-ready UI and website designs. It’s still in beta, yet it’s already replacing expensive design tools for many creators.

• Opal — Think n8n or Make, but with Google AI built in. Just describe the workflow you need, and Opal creates the automation—no coding required.

• Antigravity — An AI-powered coding workspace built on Gemini 3 Pro. Ask for an app, and the AI can plan the project, write the code, and even generate the landing page.

• Mixboard — An infinite AI canvas for images. Generate, remix, combine, and refine visuals until they match exactly what you imagined.

Branding. Design. Automation. Development. Visual creation.

Five tools. Zero subscription fees.

Meanwhile, many people are paying every month for alternatives without realizing Google already offers these for free.

Which one would you try first?

items.title: Google just dropped 15 AI tools that are completely FREE.
items.summary:
Google just dropped 15 AI tools that are completely FREE.

They’re all open source or free to use, and together they can save you hundreds (or even thousands) every month.

Bookmark this.

1. Pomelli
https://t.co/6w2sWQlrre

Turns your website into a complete brand identity, then generates matching social posts, marketing campaigns, and images.

2. Stitch
https://t.co/5VIRBUOnkw

Describe the UI you want, and it generates production-ready HTML, CSS, Tailwind, plus a Figma export.

3. Opal
https://t.co/q249sLWb8X

Create AI apps and multi-step workflows with plain English instead of code.

4. Antigravity
https://t.co/l62jKmkeaa

An AI coding workspace that can plan, edit multiple files, and build complete applications from a single prompt.

5. Mixboard
https://t.co/CwZFws2FkZ

Generate, remix, and edit AI images on an infinite canvas to create moodboards and visual concepts.

6. Disco
https://t.co/WcO4HcwbwV

Transforms your open browser tabs into interactive AI apps.

7. NotebookLM
https://t.co/KNZ0hFkBwv

Upload PDFs, videos, documents, or notes and instantly get summaries, study guides, quizzes, and even podcast-style discussions.

8. Learn Your Way
https://t.co/HFTqvtAR8s

Creates a personalized AI course on any topic with lessons, audio, quizzes, and mind maps.

9. Google AI Studio
https://t.co/HaK2oEWF3L

Prototype and build AI apps with Gemini using a free API key and a massive context window.

10. Jules
https://t.co/QoijiR6nyb

Assign it a GitHub issue and it writes the code, makes the changes, and opens a pull request.

11. Gemini CLI
https://t.co/Mx3uT1TpLk

Use Gemini from your terminal to understand your codebase, run commands, and speed up development.

12. Code Wiki
https://t.co/uw8S0vN7sw

Generate a living wiki for any public GitHub repository with architecture diagrams and AI-powered code explanations.

13. Firebase Studio
https://t.co/foXixh3ml5

An AI workspace for building backend services and cloud applications.

14. Gemini Code Assist
https://t.co/T9vhZ905aC

Google’s free AI coding assistant with AI-powered code completion, reviews, and IDE integrations.

15. Gemini Code Assist for GitHub

https://t.co/G0t5iF8R2Q

Review pull requests, explain code, and speed up development directly inside GitHub.

items.title: A 17-year-old schoolboy from Indonesia sells companies ad videos for $150 each. His cost per video is $2.60, and a watch
items.summary:
A 17-year-old schoolboy from Indonesia sells companies ad videos for $150 each. His cost per video is $2.60, and a watch shop owner could not tell his work apart from a $4,000 studio shoot

Client price: $150
Generation cost: $2.60
Software: Gemini Omni via Google AI Pro, $19.99 a month
Videos sold: 178
Revenue: $20,940
Total spend over 4 months: $1,005

The setup is simple. He takes one product photo on a white background and writes a prompt with second-by-second timecodes: [00:00] rotate from 3/4 toward front, [00:05] macro on the crown, key light from camera left. Seedance 2.0 generates it, Gemini Omni fixes the shots right in the chat.

He found the key detail on his tenth attempt. The prompt has to state hard that the product photo is the single visual reference, and that packaging text and the logo must stay crisp and correctly spelled in every frame. Without that line the model invents its own letters, and the client sees a fake.

His first client was a watch shop at a market in Surabaya. The kid sent the owner two videos and asked which one was the $4,000 studio shoot. The owner picked the wrong one, and placed his order the same evening.

A week later 9 more sellers from that market came in. A month later he was kicked out of the local videographers chat for unfair competition. He posted the screenshot of the ban on X and got 40 orders within 24 hours.

The strangest job came from a gravestone seller who needed the granite polish to look impressive. That video got 900,000 views and booked the workshop out for six months.

The money goes to his mother's card because he is under 18. For the first two months she thought it was a school scholarship.

A buyer from Dubai offered $12,000 for his prompt. He refused, and said one thing: they are not paying for the prompt, they are paying because business does not know yet that a video costs $2.60. He gives that window six more months.

While some wait for AI to get cheaper, someone is already selling a two dollar video for $150

items.title: A 17-year-old schoolboy from Indonesia sells companies ad videos for $150 each. His cost per video is $2.60, and a watch
items.summary:
A 17-year-old schoolboy from Indonesia sells companies ad videos for $150 each. His cost per video is $2.60, and a watch shop owner could not tell his work apart from a $4,000 studio shoot

Client price: $150
Generation cost: $2.60
Software: Gemini Omni via Google AI Pro, $19.99 a month
Videos sold: 178
Revenue: $20,940
Total spend over 4 months: $1,005

The setup is simple. He takes one product photo on a white background and writes a prompt with second-by-second timecodes: [00:00] rotate from 3/4 toward front, [00:05] macro on the crown, key light from camera left. Seedance 2.0 generates it, Gemini Omni fixes the shots right in the chat.

He found the key detail on his tenth attempt. The prompt has to state hard that the product photo is the single visual reference, and that packaging text and the logo must stay crisp and correctly spelled in every frame. Without that line the model invents its own letters, and the client sees a fake.

His first client was a watch shop at a market in Surabaya. The kid sent the owner two videos and asked which one was the $4,000 studio shoot. The owner picked the wrong one, and placed his order the same evening.

A week later 9 more sellers from that market came in. A month later he was kicked out of the local videographers chat for unfair competition. He posted the screenshot of the ban on X and got 40 orders within 24 hours.

The strangest job came from a gravestone seller who needed the granite polish to look impressive. That video got 900,000 views and booked the workshop out for six months.

The money goes to his mother's card because he is under 18. For the first two months she thought it was a school scholarship.

A buyer from Dubai offered $12,000 for his prompt. He refused, and said one thing: they are not paying for the prompt, they are paying because business does not know yet that a video costs $2.60. He gives that window six more months.

While some wait for AI to get cheaper, someone is already selling a two dollar video for $150
